The values change smoothly, A and B 0.46, C 0.26, then across the bridge D -0.26 and E and F -0.46, so their sign splits the graph at C–D." width="100%"} The Fiedler vector is the eigenvector of the second smallest Laplacian eigenvalue (the algebraic connectivity). It assigns each node a number such that connected nodes get similar values, while the whole vector is as spread out as possible: the smoothest non-constant labelling of the graph. Splitting nodes by sign gives a good two-way cut (`spectral_bisection()`), sorting by value gives an ordering that keeps neighbors close (`spectral_ordering()`), and plotting it reveals the graph's main axis. The vector has unit length. Its overall sign is arbitrary mathematically; EdgeCase fixes it so the first non-negligible entry (in node-ID order) is positive. Large graphs use a sparse eigensolver. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, use the normalized Laplacian. Default is `False`. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights. If `None` (default), follows the graph. Weights must be non-negative. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute to store values in. If `None` (default), uses `"fiedler_vector"`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores the values as a node attribute and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: a dictionary mapping node IDs to Fiedler vector entries. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed, disconnected, has fewer than two nodes, or has a negative weight. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} On a path, the Fiedler vector runs smoothly from one end to the other: ::: {#80874847 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec path = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(5) {n: round(v, 3) for n, v in sorted(path.fiedler_vector(return_dict=True).items())} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {1: 0.602, 2: 0.372, 3: 0.0, 4: -0.372, 5: -0.602} ``` ::: :::
